competition: New Zealand Mathematical Olympiad Committee Squad Selection Test

problems.problem:
Consider two sequences of positive integers defined as follows:
• for $n\ge 1$, $a_n=\lfloor 2^{n+1}/3\rfloor$;
• $b_1=1$ and for $n\ge 1$, $b_{2n}=2b_{2n-1}$, $b_{2n+1}=2b_{2n}+1$.
Prove that $a_n=b_n$ for all positive integers $n$.
Each point on the sides of an equilateral triangle is coloured red or blue. Must there exist a right triangle from among these points all of whose vertices have the same colour?
What is the maximum possible value of $b+c$ if positive real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ satisfy $$4a=(a+c)(b^2+ac)$$ and for which triples $(a,b,c)$ is this maximum achieved?

At a maths camp there are various groups of students who like to get together to solve problems. Somewhat unusually, any two such groups have at least one member in common. Show that it is possible to distribute straightedges and compasses among the students in such a way that at most one student gets both a straightedge and a compass, but whenever any group meets they have both tools available.

Let $A$ and $B$ be two distinct points in the plane. Which points $C$ have the property that, for any point $X$ in the plane, either $X$ is closer to $C$ than to $A$ or $X$ is closer to $C$ than to $B$?
Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $$f(f(x)+f(y))=f(x)+y$$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$.

Let $O$ be the circumcentre of acute-angled triangle $ABC$. Let $c_1$ be the circumcircle of $ABO$ and $c_2$ that of $ACO$. Let $P$ be the point on $c_1$ such that $OP$ is a diameter of $c_1$, and $Q$ the point on $c_2$ such that $OQ$ is a diameter of $c_2$. Let $T$ be the intersection of the tangent at $P$ to $c_1$ and the tangent at $Q$ to $c_2$. Let $D\ne A$ be the second point of intersection of the line $AC$ and $c_1$. Prove that $D$, $O$ and $T$ are collinear.

Michael is trying to move a counter around the cells of a $6\times 6$ grid according to the following rules:
• The counter can initially occupy any cell.
• Thereafter the counter moves alternately to a horizontally or vertically adjacent cell or jumps one cell horizontally or vertically.
• The first move is to an adjacent cell.
• The counter may never occupy the same cell twice.
His objective is for the counter to occupy every cell on the board at some point. Show him how to do it, or convince him he should stop trying.

A sequence of positive integers $a_n$ is defined as follows: $$a_0=3,\qquad a_{n+1}=(n+1)a_n-n\quad\text{for } n\ge 0.$$ Determine all positive integers $m$ such that $\gcd(m,a_n)=1$ for all $n\ge 0$.
